name: Tank Yard v1.4.0
body:
# Tank Yard v1.4.0

Design your own on-screen interface. Map triggers and scripts can now show styled widgets (messages, counters, timers, lives and menus of choices) and react to what each player picks. Pushing crates online is smooth, and dark arenas draw faster. Everything in [v1.3.0](v1.3.0.md) is included.

## UI in the workshop

- **Show UI** puts a widget on players' screens: a title, a line of text with an icon, a bar and up to four choices, each part optional. **Hide UI** takes it away again, slot by slot or all at once.
- **Five looks:** plain text with a soft shadow, a panel, a card with a colored stripe, a banner across the screen and a pill. Pick one of 13 icons, the text size, the panel's opacity, and colors for the text, panel and accent, or leave them to follow each player's light or dark theme.
- **Place it anywhere.** Top, Middle and Bottom, Left, Center and Right jump to the usual spots, and *Across* and *Down* fine-tune it. Widgets stay inside the screen at any window size and interface scale.
- **Motion.** Widgets fade, pop, slide in from the nearer side or drop from above, fade out when they go and keep their place while their text changes. **Pulse** draws the eye. With **Reduced motion** on, they appear and go without movement.
- **Live text.** `{1}`–`{8}` show counters, `{left}` the seconds before the widget goes, `{time}` the round's clock, and `{name}` and `{score}` the player's own. They update by themselves.
- **Bars** show a set amount, a counter out of a goal you choose, or the time left. Split one into up to 20 pieces for lives or charges. Bars glide to new values.
- **Choices.** Each choice sends a signal with the player who picked it as the tank that set it off, so a shop can repair, reward or fling just that player. A menu closes for the player who picks unless it stays open. Clicking a choice never fires your gun.
- **Who sees it:** everyone, including players who join later, the players in the trigger's area, or only the player that set it off. *Hide after* takes it away after a few seconds.
- 16 slots per player. A widget in a slot replaces the one before it, so a score in its own slot never gets covered by a message.
- The inspector draws a picture of the screen with the widget on it, which replays the entrance as you change it. The logic preview shows widgets over the canvas, and you can click their choices there as the test tank.
- A new **UI** palette holds Message, Counter display, Choice menu and Hide UI.
- The bundled **Arcade Hall** pack is a finished map that uses them all: a coin counter that pays a jackpot at 20, a shop that serves only the player at its counter, a vault with a countdown and a vote for the next event. Import it in the workshop to see how it's built.

## Tank that set it off

*Who* can now be **Tank that set it off**: only the tank behind what happened, wherever it is. That's the tank that crossed an area, the first tank inside a While inside area or the player who picked a choice, and it carries through signals, delays, counters and group watchers. A plate across the map can now reward just the tank that stepped on it.

## Scripts

- `tankyard.hud` widgets take `style`, `title`, `icon`, `panel`, `opacity`, `accent`, `enter`, `pulse`, `segments` and `choices`. A pick raises the new `choice` event in the pack that showed the widget, with the widget's ID as `name` and the choice, from 1, as `value`.
- Map JSON gains the `ui` and `hide_ui` actions and the `cause` value for `who`. See the [modding guide](../modding.md#ui).

## Performance

- Pushing a crate, door or other body online no longer lags behind your tank. The client moves the body with your predicted tank, as the server will, and draws it there until the server's next update agrees.
- Lights off screen no longer take the places of lights on screen, so a dark arena with many lamps keeps the ones you can see.
- Grid decor draws only the lines on screen, which made decor in large dark maps about twice as fast with software rendering.
- The server sends map widgets only when what a player sees changes, at most ten times a second, and players can pick at most ten times a second.
- Smoke-run frame timings include the time the graphics driver takes to draw each phase, so they point at real costs.

## Fixes

- Lamps no longer show a dark dot in the middle of their glow or a thin hard ring around it. The bulb is white-hot, with a soft glint.

## Compatibility

Tank Yard 1.4.0 uses protocol 30, so 1.4.0 servers and players play only with each other. Maps and packs from earlier versions open and play unchanged; maps that use Show UI, Hide UI or *Tank that set it off* need 1.4.0.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v1.3.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v1.3.0

Push doors and crates, paths that carry cover around the arena, darkness with real light, and bots that learn which tanks win. This release adds a physics layer to the Arena Workshop, a new built-in arena that uses it, and a trained driving network for bots. Everything in [v1.2.0](v1.2.0.md) is included.

## Physics in the workshop

- **Pushable bodies.** Turn any group into one solid body that tanks push by driving into it. Choose whether it slides any way, left and right, or up and down, how far it can go in each direction, its weight, a spring that brings it home, friction, bounce and whether shots knock it about. Its decor, pads and trigger areas ride along. Bodies stop at other cover and never crush a tank.
- **Paths.** Give a group a custom animation: a list of points it travels through, each with its own timing, wait, turn and curve, played once, on a loop or there and back. The canvas draws the path from where the group rests, with numbered points, a ghost of the group at the point you're editing and a dot riding it at its own pace.
- **New triggers.** **On touch** and **On release** watch a group's blocks arrive on or leave an area, so a crate on a plate can open a gate. **Shove body**, **Fling tanks**, **Blast** (outward, or inward with a negative speed), **Zoom view**, **Lighting** and **Play path** join the action list.
- **New pads.** **Ice** cuts grip so tanks slide, and a **Gravity well** draws tanks toward its middle.
- A new **Physics** palette holds ready-made pieces: Fling pad, Blast, Vortex, Crate plate, Plate release, Shove, Path, Zoom out, Nightfall, Lights on and Lightning.

## Darkness and light

- A map can start dark, tinted toward any color, and a **Lighting** trigger can change it during a round, over time and along a curve. **Go back after** returns it to what it was, which makes lightning flashes.
- Lights, the new **Spotlight** and **Beam**, particle effects with **Glow** on, hazard, portal, launch and repair pads, every tank and every shot light the floor around them. Without shader support, the darkness is a plain veil with soft light spots.
- Spotlights fade smoothly from the lamp to nothing, leave a soft pool where they land and shine from a flared lamp with glare on its lens. Lights have a halo and a glint, and beams glow at both ends with a brighter stretch drifting along them. With **Reduced motion** on, the stretch stays still.
- With **Reduced motion** on, sudden lighting changes ease in over about half a second.

## Decor and editing

- New decor shapes: Spotlight, Beam, Grid, Disc, Triangle and Hexagon, plus a **Roof** piece.
- **Near a tank** makes decor respond to your own tank: roofs that clear as you drive under them, signs that appear as you approach, and decor that grows or glows.
- Blocks of a pushable body are drawn as crates, with a frame, braces or slats and corner bolts, in the game and in the editor, so players can tell what gives way.
- Pads have bold corner brackets, and hazard and repair pads breathe slowly so they read as live from across the arena. With **Reduced motion** on, they hold still.
- Name groups. Names show in the Map tab's new group list and in every trigger summary, such as "hide group 4 (Vault gate)".
- The Map tab lists every group with what it holds and whether tanks push it, with buttons to make it start hidden, lock it while you work around it, or select all of it.
- Maps hold up to 512 pads, 2,048 decor items and 512 triggers.
- The Check tab notes a Shove body on a group that isn't pushable and a Play path with no points, with a link to each. They no longer stop a playtest.
- The [physics and lighting tutorial](../physics-tutorial.md) builds a dark yard with a push door, a crate puzzle, a ferry and a storm. The bundled **Night Works** pack is the finished map.

## New arena: Foundry

A dim, point-symmetric works floor for Free For All, team modes, Deathmatch and Sandbox. A furnace in the middle glows red and then blows tanks back every ten seconds. Conveyor belts run along the top and bottom, cranes ride back and forth on paths, and two press rooms hold repair pads behind push doors that only open inward.

## Bots

- Bots steer with a small neural network trained by self-play. Each tick it scores sixteen directions from what the bot sees along each one: walls, incoming shots, its target and other tanks. Across nine modes, network bots scored 15–55% more points a minute than bots using the older steering, died less in every mode except Co-op, and touched walls and stood still about as often. Beginner bots keep the plainer steering.
- Bots share what they learn: which tanks earn the most points per minute alive, which tanks beat which, and which upgrade paths lead to the strongest tanks. Upgrades, targets and caution follow it, more so at higher difficulties.
- That memory persists. Servers keep it in `bot_memory_file` (default `bot-memory.json`; `""` turns it off) and offline games in the data folder. Sandbox and modded matches don't teach it anything.

## Scripts and hooks

- New script commands: `play_map_path`, `set_map_lighting`, `shove_map_body` and `fling_tank`, and `map_body` to read where a body has been pushed.
- New hook actions: `map_path`, `map_light`, `map_shove` and `fling`.
- See the [modding guide](../modding.md#physics-and-lighting) for the map schema.

## Fixes

- Text no longer turns into black boxes after the window changes size in a dark arena or the workshop. Deleting a texture now clears it from the renderer's binding cache, so a font atlas that grows later is uploaded where it belongs.
- Pushed bodies keep pace with the tank pushing them, at its speed divided by the body's weight. Contact uses the same movement rule on the host and in prediction; nearby tanks cannot push across a gap, and cooperating pushers do not make a light body outrun them. Before, a tank lost contact each time the impact stopped it, and heavier crates crept along at about a third of the tank's speed.
- **Select** in the Map tab's group list switches to Edit, so the group can be dragged right away, and opens its settings from the top.
- Palette hints for pieces near the right of the dock stay clear of the inspector.
- Client prediction moves sliding bodies forward while replaying inputs, so pushing a body online doesn't stutter.
- Game data sent to players always leaves out map triggers and paths, which the server runs, so a map with logic can't produce data a client can't read.
- The Check tab no longer says a group nothing moves when a path moves it.
- Light cones, beams and glints use fixed mesh storage instead of allocating each frame. Lighting clipped outside the window no longer darkens the whole screen.
- Roof stripes keep their angle and spacing on tall or wide pieces instead of bunching into a dark wedge.
- A damaged bot-memory file cannot stall startup by acting as a named pipe.
- Release packages include Night Works and Switchyard, with both checked alongside the other example packs.
- Connectivity checks ignore bodies and groups that triggers hide or move, so maps with push doors and gates validate.

## Compatibility

Protocol **29**. Tank Yard 1.3.0 clients and servers play only with each other; update both together. Clients from 1.2.0 and earlier receive an update message. Maps and packs from earlier versions load unchanged, and maps that use the new pieces need 1.3.0.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v1.2.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v1.2.0

Type exact values in the workshop, use team symbols with your preferred colors, and adjust effects volume while sounds are playing. This release also fixes trigger arrivals, creator-boss abilities, connection stalls and unsafe asset loading. Everything in [v1.1.0](v1.1.0.md) is included.

## Workshop and controls

- Click a slider's value to type a number, calculation such as `4000/2`, or a relative change such as `+=50`. Enter applies, Escape cancels, and Tab or Shift+Tab moves between fields. Invalid values stay in the field without changing the map or setting.
- Hold Shift while dragging a slider for finer control. Fractional dimensions and plugin Number values keep their precision even when the slider has a coarse drag step; counts and color channels remain whole numbers.
- The inspector scrolls focused numbers into view and supports a draggable scrollbar, Page Up/Down, Home and End. Color controls accept `#RGB` and `#RRGGBB`.
- Multi-selection adds **Space X/Y evenly** and **Match widest/tallest**. Each arrangement is one undo step, and separately submitted numbers have separate undo steps.
- Numeric input takes priority over editor and gameplay shortcuts. Clicking away applies a valid edit; an invalid edit stays focused.
- Render scale keeps exact typed percentages, such as 123%, after saving and restarting.

See the [workshop guide](../map-editor.md) and [editor plugin guide](../editor-plugins.md) for controls and examples.

## Accessibility and audio

- Choose **Red/green**, **Blue/yellow** or **Separated** palettes with a live preview. Team symbols can also stay enabled with the original colors, including on captured objectives and the minimap.
- Accessibility reset restores those options, interface scale, high contrast and reduced motion without changing other settings.
- Tank previews and their textures stay aligned when enlarged menus scroll.
- **Effects volume** controls map sounds, boss alarms and pocket ambience. Master and Effects volume now adjust map sounds already playing, including workshop previews.
- Sound samples are prepared in the background and cached individually. Repeated cues coalesce, overlapping playback is bounded, and alarm pitch changes keep a continuous waveform.
- Audio-device failures use bounded retries and distinguish microphone errors from speaker errors. A microphone failure no longer stops healthy playback.

## Gameplay and stability

- Motions with very short return delays correctly report both their outward and return arrivals to **On arrive** triggers.
- Axiom clears transient class effects when changing form. Its underlying tank ability cannot activate during creator-boss form, in either server simulation or prediction.
- Fully obstructed creator-boss attacks leave their cooldown available. Repulse can clear nearby hostile shots at the projectile limit, and Reforge explains when the hull is already full.
- Boss drones reuse squared target distances instead of repeatedly calculating square roots while choosing a target.
- Non-ASCII community passwords no longer crash when shortened to the byte limit. Settings use private file permissions on Unix and replace the previous profile only after a complete write.

## Security and connections

- SVG mod assets cannot load images from files outside the pack, including through nested SVG data URLs. Keep SVG images self-contained; external file references are ignored.
- Pack and project readers reject special files that could stall loading. Directory packs enforce their entry limit while scanning, including ignored metadata files.
- Client WebSocket and TLS upgrades have an absolute handshake deadline, preventing slow replies from keeping connection workers occupied indefinitely. Established connections continue normally after that deadline.
- Status probes process incoming datagrams in bounded batches, so a flood of invalid replies cannot prevent a probe from finishing.

## Compatibility

Protocol **28** is unchanged. Tank Yard 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 clients and servers play together; updating both sides gives you the simulation fixes as well as the client improvements. Existing maps, packs and settings remain supported. Clients from 1.0.1 and earlier still need to update.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v1.1.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v1.1.0

The Arena Workshop gains effects: decor that floats, sways, pulses, changes color and grows, launch pads, sounds and screen shake. Bacteria's pocket dimension becomes a maze of rooms with doubles that hunt you down. Scripts and JSON packs can use every new piece. Everything in [v1.0.1](v1.0.1.md) is included.

## Workshop effects

- **Animate decor** plays a looping animation on a group's decor: **Bob**, **Sway**, **Throb**, **Shake** or **Orbit**, each with its own size and pace. The five play together, so one group can bob and sway at once, and changing the pace never makes it jump.
- **Tint decor** mixes a color into a group's decor, lights and particles. A short tint that goes back makes a flash.
- **Scale decor** draws a group's decor and emitters from 0 to 400% of their placed size, particles included.
- **Stop group** halts a group's moves, turns, fades, tints, sizes and animations where they are and cancels its trip back.
- **Shake screen** shakes the views of the tanks inside a trigger's area. Players' **Camera shake** setting scales it, and Reduced motion turns it off.
- **Play sound** plays one of eight sounds at a trigger: Chime, Bell, Alarm, Switch, Whoosh, Rumble, Fanfare and Thump. Players hear it by distance, at their Effects volume.
- Tint, Scale and Animate play like motions, with a length, an easing curve and **Go back after**. **On arrive** watches them too.
- **Launch pads** fling tanks along their direction, then let them coast for a moment before steering takes over. Prediction uses the server's own code, so launches feel immediate online.
- A new **Effects** tab in the palette holds thirteen ready-made pieces: Float, Sway, Throb, Orbit, Quiver, Flash, Alarm, Dye, Grow, Stop, Quake, Chime and Siren.
- The logic preview plays effects: the canvas shakes when the test tank is caught in a Shake screen, and Play sound triggers play through your speakers.
- Effects change only how decor looks. Blocks, pads and trigger areas keep their shape and place, and Reduced motion holds animations still while keeping colors and sizes.

## Bacteria

- The pocket dimension is now a grid of rooms with aligned walls. Doorways use several positions along the room grid, and the walls continue past the edge of the maze.
- Soft, translucent ceiling lights hang above your tank with a gentle parallax. A few fixtures flicker and some have died.
- Up to three doubles of your tank wake after a short pause and follow you through the rooms. If one catches you, you're forced out early. They don't shoot, and only the server moves them.
- Bacteria's model has new shoulder plates that leave your team color visible.

## Modding

- New script functions: `tint_map_group`, `scale_map_group`, `animate_map_group`, `stop_map_group`, `shake_view` and `play_sound`, and `map_pose` to read where a group's motions have put it.
- JSON hooks gain `map_tint`, `map_animate`, `map_stop`, `shake_view` and `play_sound`, and `map_motion` accepts `scale`.
- JSON maps gain the `launch` pad and the `tint`, `scale`, `animate`, `stop`, `shake` and `sound` trigger actions. New fields are left out of exported maps when unused.
- Workshop plugins see the new trigger fields, and `editor.free_group` skips groups that effects use.
- A new example pack, [`mods/arena_fx`](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/tree/v1.1.0/mods/arena_fx), rings a bell at the start of each round, marks wrecks and kill streaks, and gives maps an alarm they can sound by name.

## Tutorials

- The [workshop guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.1.0/docs/map-editor.md#effects) covers every effect and palette piece.
- The [motions tutorial](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.1.0/docs/motions-tutorial.md) adds a step that gives the gatehouse a launch pad, a floating lantern, a door chime and a tremor as the barricades land.
- A new [Animate and effects walkthrough](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.1.0/docs/effects-tutorial.md) has matching playable site examples and a bundled [Effects Lab map](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/tree/v1.1.0/mods/effects_lab) you can play or import into the workshop.

## Sandbox and hosting

- Sandbox has a centered toolbox with tank previews, search by name or ID, tier filters, touchpad paging and separate player and spawn controls. Escape closes it, and search input takes priority over gameplay shortcuts.
- Dedicated hosts can create a token-authenticated config with `--secure --write-config`, check it with `--check-config`, and issue short-lived UDP invitations with `--issue-token`. Keys are never printed, and existing credential files are never replaced.
- Invalid private config errors no longer quote credential lines.
- The multiplayer load tool supports runs up to 24 hours, scheduled reconnects and JSON reports, with bounded timing storage.
- Local crash reports survive the next launch. `tankyard --diagnostics-path` prints their folder; reports are never uploaded automatically.
- Menu pages and bot decision subsystems are split into smaller modules. Additional sandbox checks cover hostile effect arguments, module cycles, path escapes and isolation between packs.

## Compatibility

Protocol **28** carries the doubles and the new effects. Update clients, servers and any separate relays together; 1.0.1 and earlier cannot join a 1.1.0 server, and older peers receive an update notice. Maps from earlier versions open unchanged. Maps that use launch pads or effects need 1.1.0 to open and play.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v1.0.1
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v1.0.1

Bacteria slips into a private pocket dimension, the motions tutorial has a video, and doors and returning motions behave more reliably. Everything in [v1.0.0](v1.0.0.md) is included.

## Bacteria

- A new level-55 tank, reached from Specter or Wisp, with twin alternating cannons and a **ten-second pocket dimension**.
- The entry sound and brief blackout lead into a private, Backrooms-inspired maze with yellow wallpaper, worn carpet, fluorescent lights and eerie room tones. Ceiling fixtures pass above the tank, with light pools on the carpet and slight parallax. The textures and recorded light hum are CC0 assets.
- Repair 40% of your maximum hull health over the visit and reposition through the maze. You cannot fight, take damage or capture objectives inside. Carried cores drop and deployed weapons clear on entry.
- The cooldown is 40 seconds from entry, leaving thirty seconds outside between visits. A countdown and a small return ring announce your return.
- Sounds are local, follow volume settings and fade on return. Reduced motion keeps lights steady. [Bacteria guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.0.1/docs/bacteria.md).

## Workshop

- Doors and faders with **Go back after** return home even if another tank arrives while they are open or on their way back. A new arrival extends the wait without moving the resting point.
- The palette's **Door** moves its group to a fixed offset, so repeated arrivals keep it open at the same place.
- **On arrive** no longer acts when a motion has nowhere to go, such as a door told to open while it is already open. An interrupted motion still does not count as arriving.
- Particles' **Fade out** now controls their fade.
- Motion destinations and portal exits have diamond handles, matching the editor's guides.

## Tutorials

- The [motions tutorial](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.0.1/docs/motions-tutorial.md) builds a gatehouse with a sliding door, moving cover, chained motions, lights and particles.
- Its [video](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.0.1/docs/motions-tutorial.mp4) runs for 2 minutes 15 seconds, with English captions and seven chapters on the [website](https://robertflexx.github.io/tankyard-site/#motions-video). Choose **Motions** above the workshop's player.
- The website's [interactive motions guide](https://robertflexx.github.io/tankyard-site/#motions) demonstrates every curve and mode, all ten Motion pieces, chained motions, lights and particle presets.

## Compatibility

Protocol **27** adds the pocket timer and ability. Update clients, servers and any separate relays together; 1.0.0 and earlier cannot join a 1.0.1 server. Older peers receive an update notice. Existing 1.0 maps open unchanged.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v1.0.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v1.0.0

Tank Yard 1.0 is here: sliding doors, lifts and moving cover glide in the workshop, lights glow like real lamps, particles gain new shapes, and tanks and bosses look sharper.

Thank you to everyone who played, hosted, built maps and reported bugs on the way here.

## Motions

- Four new trigger actions animate a group. **Move group** glides it by a distance, and **Move group to** glides it to a place measured from where the map puts it. **Turn decor** and **Fade decor** turn or fade its decor. A group's blocks, pads, decor and trigger areas move together, and moving cover pushes tanks, shapes and bosses out of its way.
- Each motion has a length, one of eleven easing curves (Linear, Sine, Quad, Cubic, Quart, Quint, Expo, Circ, Back, Elastic and Bounce) and a mode (ease in, ease out, in and out, out and in). The Object tab draws the curve and plays it. **Go back after** plays the motion in reverse later, for doors that shut and lifts that come back down.
- **On arrive** acts when a group's motion ends, so motions can follow one another: a lift rises, then its door opens.
- Select a Move trigger to see where it sends its group, and drag the diamond to set the distance. The logic preview plays motions and outlines where each moved group belongs.
- The new **Motion** tab in the palette holds ready-made Door, Shuttle, Piston, Lift, Home, Drop, Spinner, Fader, Blink and Then pieces.
- Scripts can call `move_map_group`, `turn_map_group` and `fade_map_group`, and JSON hooks have a `map_motion` action.
- Moving cover adds almost no network traffic: snapshots carry each motion rather than every wall's position, and every client plays the same glide. Bots re-plan their routes while cover moves.

The [workshop guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.0.0/docs/map-editor.md#motions) explains motions, and the [modding guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v1.0.0/docs/modding.md#motions) has the map format.

## Lights and particles

- Lights brighten what lies under them: strongly in dark arenas and softly in light ones. **Flicker** makes a light waver like a flame or a failing lamp. The Decor tab has new Torch, Neon and Lantern presets.
- Particles can be soft or star-shaped, glow, drift sideways and twinkle. They can start anywhere in the emitter, inside its ellipse, along its outline or at its center. There are six new presets: Fireflies, Smoke, Snow, Glitter, Fountain and Pulse.
- Maps crowded with lights draw the extra ones more simply rather than slowing the frame, as maps crowded with particles already did.

## Workshop

- The workshop remembers your palette tab and item, the inspector tab, the Hidden and Animate switches, the logic preview's speed and where you were looking in the map, along with panel sizes.
- **Ctrl+Shift+A** selects everything like the selection, such as every torch or every speed pad.

## Tanks and bosses

- Automatic turrets sharing one mount are drawn as a single turret with a ringed cap, so their barrels no longer cross over each other. Fortress Array, Palisade, Tri-Sniper, Interceptor and Monolith look much cleaner.
- Boss armor has a raised rim. Wounded bosses glow amber, then pulse red in their last phase. Defender's turrets no longer cross over one another.

## Other changes

- On FreeBSD, the graphics settings explain that NVIDIA ships DLSS only for Linux and Windows.
- `tankyard-models --bosses --phase 3` draws bosses in a later phase.
- In workshop plugins, `editor.free_group` skips groups that motions and On arrive triggers use.
- Creator and central-owner identities are verified without asking only on the official server, servers on the same computer and games you host. Any other server asks first, so a server cannot pass your proof on to another server without your consent.

## Compatibility

Protocol **26**. Servers and players on 1.0 play only with each other, so players on 0.15 or 0.16 need to update before joining. Hosts should update their servers and relays together. Maps from earlier versions open unchanged, but maps saved or exported from 1.0 need 1.0.
